title: First Value Pathway - 90 Day Plan
summary: Compact, pragmatic 90-day onboarding plan focused on driving measurable first value for teams integrating Redwood inference. Designed for technical product teams evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Includes milestone acceptance criteria, communication cadence, renewal triggers, and quick playbook snippets.
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, action-focused template to get customers to measurable first value within 30 days and predictable sustained usage by day 90. Written as a working document for CS owners running technical onboarding for teams integrating Redwood Inference APIs or Private deployments.

Who this is for:
- Technical PM or engineering lead integrating inference (LLM features)
- CS Owner + Solutions Engineer pairing
- Typical customer: SaaS product team, internal platform, or enterprise product team with regulatory constraints

North Star / Primary success metrics (tie to customer outcomes):
- Day-7: Successful auth + run of a canonical request (sample prompt) against the chosen deployment (hosted/api-key or dedicated/private connection).
- Day-30: First Value Metric — feature prototype in staging serving real test traffic (>= 100 requests/day) with accepted output quality by product owner.
- Day-60: Performance SLOs measured & met in staging: p95 latency <= agreed target, error rate <1%, unit cost within budgeted threshold.
- Day-90: Production rollout to initial user cohort with playback monitoring and rollback plan; renewal signal if usage and quality meet contract thresholds.

Acceptance criteria (example definitions):
- Auth: API key rotation tested OR VPC peering validated and sample call passes with customer certs.
- Correctness: 10 prompt pairs (golden set) pass rubric score >= 0.8 for quality or otherwise documented tradeoffs.
- Reliability: Synthetic load test showing sustained throughput at 2x expected baseline with no increased error rate.
- Cost: Token spend forecast for month 2 <= budget cap; sample batching reduces token-cost per call by >=15% if applicable.

30-day plan (Goals + tasks) — "Get to first usable feature"
Week 0 (Kickoff)
- Kickoff meeting (CS + SE + Customer Eng Lead): align success metrics, timeline, primary contacts.
- Share quickstart: API keys, sample prompts, example SDK usage.
- Deliverables: shared spreadsheet with endpoints, test prompts, and access details.

Week 1
- Validate connectivity: call /v1/generate (hosted) or smoke test on Dedicated/Private endpoint. Capture latencies, error codes.
- Create the golden prompt set (10 examples) covering typical failure modes.
- Setup basic observability: logs, trace hook, token-cost dashboard (console.csv export or direct dashboard link).

Week 2
- Prototype integration: embed basic feature (search summarization, chat flow, text completion) in staging.
- Run qualitative review with product owner against golden set; iterate.
- Short checklist: confirm KV cache warmup behavior on sample flows, checkpoint for batching settings.

Week 3-4
- Stabilize prototype: address top 3 failure modes, add retry/timeout logic to client, confirm streaming path if used.
- Run light load test (50–200 rps synthetic) to observe latency tails and throughput.
- Customer sign-off on first-value milestone or list of open items and owners.

60-day plan (Goals + tasks) — "Performance & Quality Harden"
- Instrument detailed metrics: token-level cost breakdown, model-by-route latency, per-route error rates.
- Perform an eval sweep vs baseline model(s); capture regression signals and create an action list.
- Decide model and quantization strategy for production (e.g., high-quality open model vs quantized lower-cost variant).
- Rollout policy: configure canary with 5–10% traffic and rollback hooks in Console.
- Security checklist: confirm audit logging, KMS integration if required, and any data retention settings.

90-day plan (Goals + tasks) — "Production readiness & renewal prep"
- Production rollout to target cohort with monitoring dashboards and runbooks.
- Validate cost projections vs actual usage; flag need for quotas/alerts.
- Run a post-launch review: quality metrics, customer NPS check, business metric impact.
- Renewal trigger evaluation: customer meets usage threshold X, product owner confirms positive ROI signal Y, SLA needs confirmed.

Stakeholder map (example):
- Product Owner (customer) — owns acceptance of first-value feature
- Engineering Lead (customer) — integration engineering tasks owner
- CS Owner (Redwood) — project manager, renewal liaison
- Solutions Engineer (Redwood) — technical runbook, load testing, model tuning
- Security/Compliance (customer) — sign-off for private deploy or KMS

Communication cadence (recommended):
- Weekly tactical standup (30 min) with bullet updates + owners for open tickets
- Biweekly demo with product owner showing feature improvements and metrics
- Slack channel for async questions + a single-threaded email for executive updates

Risk register & mitigations (quick list):
- Risk: Output quality below expectation -> Mitigation: add reranking/eval run, tune prompts, propose model variant; schedule joint QA session immediately.
- Risk: Latency spikes at tail -> Mitigation: enable smaller batching and autoscale, DB/IO review, RTC for long prompts.
- Risk: Cost exceeds forecast -> Mitigation: enable caching, enforce rate limits, suggest quantized model.
- Risk: Private network/connectivity issues -> Mitigation: run a connectivity playbook, confirm firewall rules and sample curl flows.

Renewal / Expansion signals (heuristics to track):
- Stable daily active feature usage for 14 consecutive days post-production.
- Customer successfully runs an eval suite without regressions for 2 weeks.
- Latency & error rate meet agreed SLOs for 30 days.
- Product owner expresses plans to expand to additional routes or increase concurrency.

Playbook snippets (copyable):
- Kickoff agenda: 1) Goals & metrics 2) Roles & contacts 3) Quickstart steps 4) Risks & timeline 5) Next steps
- Sample 7-day check-in email: "Quick status: auth verified, prototype running with sample prompts, observed p95 Xms. Next: seed golden dataset + performance run. Any blockers?"
- Canary rollback steps: 1) Disable canary route in Console 2) Re-route to baseline model 3) Re-run failing prompts offline and triage

Checklist (one-page view) — items to tick:
- [ ] API/auth smoke test passed
- [ ] Golden prompt set created and evaluated
- [ ] Basic dashboards wired (latency, errors, token cost)
- [ ] Prototype in staging with product owner sign-off
- [ ] Load test executed and tail latencies documented
- [ ] Security/compliance checklist completed for deployment type
- [ ] Canary configured with rollback plan
- [ ] Renewal signals tracker added to CRM (renewal score + comments)

Notes to CS Owner (working):
- Keep communications simple for non-engineering execs: highlight "time-to-first-value" + projected monthly cost.
- For Dedicated customers, early capacity sizing reduces late surprises; ask for expected concurrency early in wk1.
- For Private customers, root cause: network/firewall config is 40% of delays in our last 8 onboardings; prioritize a pre-kickoff network checklist.

Open items / TODOs
- Build a small shared script bundle that runs smoke tests across hosted/dedicated/private and writes a simple pass/fail report (associate with JIRA CS-398).
- Add templated golden prompt sets for common use cases: summarization, retrieval-augmented generation, chat assistants.
- Create a short one-pager for execs that maps adoption milestones to renewal conversation triggers.

Appendix (quick references)
- Example golden-prompt rubric: precision, helpfulness, hallucination score, latency and token cost.
- Useful links: onboarding scripts repo, Console dashboard setup guide, canary rollout doc.

-- end working draft --

(Notes: this is intentionally concise — use as a skeleton; copy relevant sections into a customer-specific doc and replace the sample thresholds with contract-specific numbers.)
